## Why This Is Asked

This question validates practical debugging skills for containerized RHCSA-level infrastructure. It covers TLS termination with SNI routing, mTLS to upstream backends, and production-readiness concerns including SELinux policy enforcement, firewall rules, and zero-downtime service upgrades.

## Key Concepts

- **TLS termination in Podman containers** using SNI for multi-tenant routing
- **mTLS configuration** between reverse proxy and backends, including CA validation
- **SELinux policy considerations** for networking, port binding, and proxy operations
- **nftables firewall rules** for controlling ingress and egress traffic
- **Systemd drop-ins** for graceful service reloads and zero-downtime deployments

## Common Pitfalls

Candidates often miss the distinction between `systemctl restart` (which drops connections) and `systemctl reload` (which maintains them). They may also overlook SELinux denials as a root cause, or fail to verify both inbound firewall rules and outbound rules to backend servers.

## Why This Is Asked

Tests comprehensive production-grade auditing capabilities: real-time file monitoring, secure centralized log collection, and automated integrity verification.

## Key Concepts

- auditd file monitoring using watch rules (-w) with permission tracking (-p)
- audisp-remote TLS encryption for secure log forwarding
- AIDE baseline initialization and scheduled verification
- systemd timer automation for daily integrity checks
- End-to-end audit pipeline validation

## Code Example

```javascript
# Audit rules configuration
sudo dnf install -y audit
sudo systemctl enable auditd --now

# Create monitoring rules
cat > /etc/audit/rules.d/critical-files.rules << 'EOF'
-w /etc/ssh/sshd_config -p wa -k ssh_config
-w /etc/nsswitch.conf -p wa -k nsswitch_config  
-w /etc/passwd -p wa -k passwd_config
EOF

# Load rules and restart auditd
sudo auditctl -R /etc/audit/rules.d/critical-files.rules
sudo systemctl restart auditd
```

## Implementation Approach

Establish file-level monitoring with auditd, configure secure remote log aggregation, deploy AIDE for baseline integrity, and automate verification cycles while ensuring comprehensive audit trail coverage.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests systemd mastery: timers, dependencies, failure handling, and idempotent logging.

## Key Concepts
- systemd timer and service wiring
- network-online.target dependency
- OnFailure retry flow
- centralized log rotation for backup logs

## Code Example
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.service
[Unit]
Description=Nightly backup
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/daily-backup.sh
StandardOutput=append:/var/log/backup.log
StandardError=append:/var/log/backup.log
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.timer
[Unit]
Description=Daily backup timer

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily 02:00
Persistent=true
Unit=backup.service

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup.service.d/override.conf
[Unit]
OnFailure=backup-retry.service
```
```ini
# /etc/systemd/system/backup-retry.service
[Unit]
Description=Retry backup after failure
After=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 900; /usr/local/bin/daily-backup.sh'
```
```ini
# /etc/logrotate.d/backup
/var/log/backup.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
}
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine systemd scheduling (service + timer), non-root privileges, archiving backups with date suffix, and log rotation for maintainability.

## Key Concepts
- systemd service and timer
- non-login user and file permissions
- tar with date suffix
- logrotate configuration and rotation policies

## Code Example
```bash
# Create non-root user
useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin appback

# Backup script
cat > /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
tar czf /var/backups/app-backup-$(date +%F).tar.gz /home/app >> /var/log/app-backup.log 2>&1
EOF
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh
chown appback:appback /usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh

# Systemd service
cat > /etc/systemd/system/app-backup.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=App backup script

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=appback
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/backup-app.sh
EOF

# Systemd timer
cat > /etc/systemd/system/app-backup.timer <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Daily app backup timer

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
EOF

# Logrotate
cat > /etc/logrotate.d/app-backup <<'EOF'
/var/log/app-backup.log {
  daily
  rotate 7
  compress
  missingok
  notifempty
}
EOF

# Enable and test
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now app-backup.timer
```
